mathematical_review.topic: All prescribed centers and all half-widths
mathematical_review.finding: odd_count_fixed_center_bound quantifies over every List Symbol and every Fin 10 center, with empty width handled reflexively, widths one through three by exhaustive kernel reductions over exact transition classes, and larger widths by established coordinatewise domination.

nines_fixed_center_formula gives the all-nine target count exactly as oddCenterMax. Together with the universal bound this proves an exact fixed-center maximum. leading_eleven_exact_center attains the same count at every positive half-width and each prescribed center.

Writing integer differences x=a-d and y=b-c, the all-nine update sends (x,y) to (-y,x+y). The exact phase list starting at (1,0) is (1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1). Thus the even-minus-odd endpoint difference is 1,1,0,-1,-1,0. This justifies ceiling on even centers in residues 0,1,2 and on odd centers in residues 3,4,5, with ties at residues 2 and 5.

sharpCenter chooses 6 for residues below three and 7 otherwise. Its parity selects the maximum endpoint and its value is always at least five. At half-width zero, the exact enumerator is [([],6)], with Center 6 0 6 verified independently.

A prescribed center can have no preimages: oddCenterMax 1 7=0 and oddPreimages [11] 7 0=[]. The universal fixed-center maximum statements correctly permit this case; they do not assert existence for every center.

The reviewed objects count source coefficient-word encodings (xs,z), not arbitrary decimal digit decompositions or distinct original integers. Complete actual normalization correspondence and canonical-positive filtering are supplied by separate modules. Positive source exteriors for the leading-eleven family follow from the previously reviewed core positivity theorem; no new arbitrary-width positivity assumption is hidden here.

The extension proves sharpCenter_large and exact sharp counts. The informal consequence for a subsequent arithmetic step depends on the separate actual semantics wrapper; the review does not classify the counting extension alone as an orbit or nonpalindrome theorem.
